questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 38 degrees. What is the size of each base angle?
The angles of a triangle are (2x + 5) degrees, (3x - 10) degrees, and (x + 35) degrees. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle sum to 180: (2x + 5) + (3x - 10) + (x + 35) = 180. So 6x + 30 = 180, giving x = 25. The three angles are 55, 65, and 60 degrees. The largest is 65 degrees.

questions.stem: In triangle PQR, side QR is extended to point S. Angle P = 52 degrees and angle Q = 73 degrees. What is the exterior angle PRS?
questions.explanation: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles. Angle PRS = 52 + 73 = 125 degrees.

questions.stem: In an isosceles triangle, one of the base angles is 68 degrees. What is the apex angle?
questions.explanation: Both base angles are 68 degrees. Apex angle = 180 - 68 - 68 = 44 degrees.

questions.stem: A right-angled isosceles triangle has a hypotenuse of 10 cm. What are the other two angles?
questions.explanation: A right-angled isosceles triangle has one 90-degree angle and two equal angles. The two equal angles = (180 - 90) / 2 = 45 degrees each.
